newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian parliament to take up test motion on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Indian parliament to take up test motion on Friday.

text.p: India's lower house of parliament, the Lok Sabha, is scheduled to convene at 11 a.m. (0630 GMT) on Friday to take up a confidence motion in Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.

The Lok Sabha is expected to debate the motion before taking any vote. No time has been set for the vote. The speaker of the house, P.A. Sangma, has said the debate and vote will be shown live on nationwide television.
Deve Gowda would need a simple majority of legislators present and voting to win the test of strength.
The 545-seat lower house of parliament, the Lok Sabha, currently has 542 members. Two seats are vacant and one is occupied by the speaker, Sangma, who can vote in the event of a tie.
General elections in April and May last year yielded a hung parliament.
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is the biggest single party with 162 deputies. With its four allies, the BJP controls 193 votes -- well shy of an absolute majority.

Deve Gowda's 15-party United Front coalition controls 180 votes. Its strongest component is the prime minister's centrist Janata Dal party with 45 legislators, followed by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) with 32.
Deve Gowda has been propped up by the Congress party, which controls 140 votes but withdrew its backing on Sunday.
A quorum of at least 55 members of parliament would have to be present for the vote of confidence to be taken, a parliament spokesman said.
The BJP held power for 12 days in May but quit when it failed to muster enough support to win a vote of confidence.
